segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus walked the borderland between Samaria and Galilee — the seam between two peoples who despised each other. Keep that seam in mind. It matters at the end of this story.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he reached a village, ten men met him — but they stopped far off, strung along a rise, and came no closer. They were lepers. The Law of Moses required them to live outside the town and to warn everyone away. That gap of empty ground between them and the road was not shyness. It was the law. These were ten men no one had touched in years.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they did the only thing the distance left them. They lifted up their voices together and called across the gap: Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he saw them, he did not close the distance. He did not touch them, and he did not announce that they were healed. He simply gave them an instruction:

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Go shew yourselves unto the priests.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now, why send them to a priest? Because in Israel the priest was the only inspector who could certify a leper clean and let him back into his family, his work, his worship. Sending them was a promise in disguise. That errand only made sense one way: if they would be clean by the time they arrived.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But nothing had changed yet. They looked at each other, at their own still-bandaged hands, at the long road to a city they had no proof they would be welcome in. And then, one by one, they turned and started walking anyway.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And as they went — on the road, mid-step, in the middle of obeying, before there was one thing to see — they were made clean.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The linen loosened and fell. New skin underneath. Nine of them ran on toward the city, toward the priests, toward their old lives handed back. But one of them, when he saw what had happened to him, stopped in the road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he turned around. He came back the way he came, running, praising God at the top of his voice — the whole road hearing it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He threw himself face-down in the dust at Jesus's feet and poured out his thanks. And Luke adds one detail that would have stunned everyone listening: he was a Samaritan. The outsider. The one the religion of the day said did not belong.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at the empty road where the other nine had gone, and asked:

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Except this stranger. This outsider. This is not wounded pride — the nine did nothing wrong. They obeyed, and they were healed, every one of them. His question is grief, not a scolding: they got the gift and kept walking, and they missed the giver. Only the one everyone counted out came back to find him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus reached down to the man still trembling at his feet, and lifted him with a word:

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Hear the two different words. All ten were cleansed — out on the road, before any of them said thank you. But only this one, the one who came back, was made whole. Cleansed happened to his skin. Whole happened to all of him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he rose and walked home a whole man, the old wrappings left behind him in the road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The healing happened while they walked, before they could see it. Have you ever had to move forward on nothing but a word — before there was any proof?
